title: Approval rules of 21 Oct: no levels = no approval; costing-based quotes approved once; levels at the same time

steps.do: Set up Sales → note your levels, then Remove every level. As Test BDM make a ₹1,00,000 quotation and press Submit for approval.
steps.expect: "No approval is needed for this quote — your company has no approval levels. It is ready to send." Status Approved. Put your levels back afterwards (SAL-003).
steps.observed: All 3 levels removed. The ₹1,00,000 quotation Q-00001 offers no "Submit for approval" button: it stays DRAFT; its Actions bar reads "Actions — move this quote: ✉ Send to client No approval needed — your company has no approval levels. Mark lost 🧮 Project costing: ＋ Create costing for this quotation Pre-order review 5/5 done Enquir" (a "Send to client" button straight from the draft). The message "No approval is needed for this quote — your company has no approval levels. It is ready to send." and the Approved status never appear.

steps.do: With the levels back: make a project costing from an enquiry (SAL-050), get it approved (SAL-051), "Make a quotation" from it, change nothing, Submit for approval.
steps.expect: "No approval is needed … it is at the prices of its approved project costing, which the approval levels already signed." Status Approved — no second round.
steps.observed: Costing approved by Test BranchMgr and Test MktMgr; "Create quotation" made Q-00002. It offers no "Submit for approval": it stays DRAFT; its Actions bar reads "Actions — move this quote: ✉ Send to client No approval needed — it is at the prices of its approved project costing, which the approval levels already signed. Mark lost 🧮 Project costing: AHM/PC/2026-27/11/0001 Rev 00 " (a "Send to client" button straight from the draft). The expected message and the Approved status never appear.

steps.do: Make another quotation from the same costing; as its creator change one rate, with the note the screen asks for; Submit.
steps.expect: It is approved (step 2), so it is changed through Edit → "Create revision" (owner, 15 Nov 2026, F19). The new revision has its own costing revision, which is approved first; then it goes to the approval levels like any quotation (the price is no longer the costing's).
steps.observed: On the first quotation (the costing no longer offers "Create quotation" once one is made from it): changing a rate first asked "This quote was priced from costing AHM/PC/2026-27/11/0001 Rev 00. Say why its prices now differ, in "Why the prices diff…"; with the note it saved, and Submit sent it to the levels: "Submitted for approval — 2 step(s). Now with Test BranchMgr (Branch Manager); then, last, level 2: Test MktMgr (Marketing Manager)." (levels 1, 2).
steps.reason: The costing page stops offering "Create quotation" once one quotation has been made from it, so "another quotation from the same costing" cannot be made; the rate change was tested on the first one.
steps.proposed: One approved costing prices one quotation. A price change is made on that quotation by its creator, with the note asked for, and it then goes to the approval levels like any quotation — as observed.

steps.do: Set up Sales → "When a quote needs more than one level, how do the levels approve?" → "At the same time — every level but the top one at once; the top one last" → Save these answers.
steps.expect: Saved. The escalation question now notes it is used only one after another.
steps.observed: "Saved. 1 answer changed — it applies from now on."; the escalation question notes "(One after another only — at the same time, the levels are all asked already.)"

steps.do: As Test BDM submit a ₹6,00,000 quotation with three levels, the top one a Business Director. Sign in as Test MktMgr (level 2) → Approvals.
steps.expect: It is listed straight away — level 2 does not wait for level 1 (unless one reports to the other). The quotation reads "Now with level 1: …; level 2: … (at the same time); then, last, level 3: <Business Director>". (From 14 Nov 2026 top management always signs last — SAL-192.)
steps.observed: With the SAL-003 levels a ₹6,00,000 quotation has only two levels — ₹6,00,000 (Q-00003): 2 levels (BRANCH_MANAGER, MARKETING_MANAGER); "Submitted for approval — 2 step(s). Now with Test BranchMgr (Branch Manager); then, last, level 2: Test MktMgr (Marketing Manager)."; on Test MktMgr's Approvals straight away: no (its top level, the Marketing Manager, now signs last, owner 14 Nov 2026). With three levels (₹30,00,000, Q-00004) it reads "Submitted for approval — 3 step(s). Now with level 1: Test BranchMgr (Branch Manager); level 2: Test MktMgr (Marketing Manager) (at the same time); then, last,
steps.suggest: As Test BDM submit a ₹30,00,000 quotation (three levels, the top one a Business Director). Sign in as Test MktMgr (level 2) → Approvals. Expect: listed straight away; the quotation reads "Now with level 1: …; level 2: … (at the same time); then, last, level 3: Test Director".

steps.do: Test MktMgr and Test BranchMgr approve, then the Business Director.
steps.expect: After the second signature: "All approvals complete — quote approved and ready to send."
steps.observed: MktMgr: "Your approval is recorded. Now with Test BranchMgr (Branch Manager); then, last, level 3: Test Director (Business Director)."; BranchMgr: "Your approval is recorded. Now with Test Director (Business Director)."; Director (last): "All approvals complete — quote approved and ready to send." — Approved.
steps.note: With three levels the "All approvals complete" message comes after the third signature (the Director's), not the second.

steps.do: Switch the answer back to "One after another" and Save.
steps.expect: Level 2 is again asked only after level 1 has signed.
steps.observed: Saved ("Saved. 1 answer changed — it applies from now on."). Q-00005 (₹10,00,000): not on Test MktMgr's Approvals until Test BranchMgr signed level 1, then listed.
